positive_change.result: Une floraison record a transformé le désert d'Atacama, sec depuis des décennies, avec environ 200 espèces de fleurs émergeant après un épisode exceptionnel de pluies.
positive_change.beneficiaries: Les plantes du désert d'Atacama ainsi que la biodiversité locale, incluant insectes pollinisateurs et certains animaux, qui profitent temporairement de cet afflux de vie.

fact_checks.sentence: Le désert d’Atacama, réputé pour être le plus sec au monde, a connu une floraison exceptionnelle en 2025, alimentée par des pluies record liées à l’épisode climatique El Niño.
source_passages: Chile’s Atacama Desert has erupted into perhaps the greatest floral display ever recorded there, with some 200 species blooming—some in areas where flowers haven’t been seen since the before new millennium.

“But it’s a race against time — this brief biological window allows these species to complete their life cycle, which lasts roughly two to three months.” This year’s Super El Niño weather event dumped record rainfall onto the landscape.

fact_checks.sentence: Environ 200 espèces de fleurs jusque-là dormantes sous la terre ont pu pousser après avoir attendu des décennies cette humidité.
source_passages: Chile’s Atacama Desert has erupted into perhaps the greatest floral display ever recorded there, with some 200 species blooming—some in areas where flowers haven’t been seen since the before new millennium.
Through July and August, flooding allowed water to permeate deep into the soil, touching seeds that normally escape seasonal rains.

fact_checks.sentence: Ce phénomène survient lorsque conditions pluviométriques et températures favorables réveillent des graines et tubercules en sommeil.
source_passages: VIDEO: 🇨🇱 Chile's Atacama Desert fills with flowers in spring The phenomenon, known as the "flowering desert," occurs in certain years when rainfall and temperatures coincide, awakening the desert's dormant seeds #AFPVertical https://t.co/Cr4C3LaFa8— AFP News Agency (@AFP) October 6, 2025 It means that seeds and tubers have lain dormant under the sand waiting for the lifegiving touch of water for decades—a remarkable adaptation.

“This is a natural seed bank, a dormant archive that becomes a living one with the rains,” Moisés Grimberg, the administrator of Llanos de Challe National Park in the Atacama, told NPR, whose images of the flowering have to be seen to be believed.

fact_checks.sentence: Ce court épisode de vie florale, qui dure deux à trois mois, offre temporairement nourriture et habitat à divers animaux locaux, notamment insectes pollinisateurs et reptiles.
source_passages: NPR says the increased frequency of the seasonal rains are creating conditions for more varied animal life—albeit transiently—such as reptiles, insects, bats and other pollinators, and even larger animals like the iconic guanaco, a relative of the lama.

“But it’s a race against time — this brief biological window allows these species to complete their life cycle, which lasts roughly two to three months.” This year’s Super El Niño weather event dumped record rainfall onto the landscape.

fact_checks.sentence: Par ailleurs, les chercheurs collectent des semences pour préserver cette diversité végétale fragile.
source_passages: This genetic mothership is the central node in a nationwide network of institutions that are safeguarding the country’s plant diversity, come what may, and its scientists aren’t wasting this opportunity to merely take photographs.
Ana Sandoval and her colleagues are busy collecting seeds generated by the now-pollinated flowers for future research.

fact_checks.sentence: Ce cycle naturel souligne l’adaptation remarquable du désert à des conditions extrêmes, tout en invitant à mieux protéger ces écosystèmes rares.
source_passages: For the people who protect this desert ecosystem, it’s another reminder of the incredible resilience and diversity of life that makes this place worth protecting.
